To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calcium alginate- pectin entrapped concavalin A-bitters gourd peroxidize complex is more stable than its free counterpart and is suitable for use as a catalyst in industrial applications.
immobilization of concanavalain A-bitter gour peroxidase complex by calcium alginate- pectin matrix enhanced thermostability, pH stability and stability against denaturing agents.
the calcium alginate- pectin entrapped concavalin A-butter gourd peroxidases are more stable than the soluble form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
immobilization of concanavalins A and bitter gourd peroxidases by entrapment in calcium alginate- pectin gel.
the development and characterization of a new biocatalytic system based on calcium alginate and pectin entrapped concavalin A-perioxidase complex.

the preparation of a stable enzyme preparation by entrapping concanavalin-A-enzyme complexes into calcium alginate-polygalacturonic acid gel beads and its application in the removal of phenol from industrial effluent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immobilization of peroxidase from bitter gourd by concanavalin-A and subsequent immobilization into calcium alginate-pectin gel matrix resulted in an enzyme preparation with improved stability.
the immobilized concanavalin-bitter gourd complex is a more stable enzyme preparation than the native form.

concanavalin a-peroxidase complex is more resistant to denaturing conditions than the native enzyme and the immobilized enzyme is more stable to denaturing conditions as compared to the native enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the calcium alginate- pectin entrapped concanaavalin A-biter gourd peroxidases can be used as a stable and efficient catalyst in the biotechnological applications.

concanavalin-A-bitter gourd-peroxidase complex was more resistant to denaturation and entrapped concavalin A-bitters gourd peroxidased was found to be more stable and retained higher fraction of original activity as compared to soluble enzyme.
concanavalin-A-bitter gourd-peroxidase complex was more stable than soluble peroxidase and the entrapped form was even more stable than the soluble and the complex forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
concanavalin-A can be used as an effective stabilizer to increase the stability of bitter gourd peroxidases.
immobilization of enzyme by entrapment in calcium alginate- pectin gel is a useful technique to enhance its stability.
immobilized peroxidases are more thermostable than soluble ones.
